aspects.says: afterExecute receives thrown == null for a submitted task; the task is the done FutureTask, which must be asked for its outcome.
basis: section:execute() Hands a Task's Exception to the Thread; submit() Keeps It in the Future

aspects.says: close() (Java 19+) shuts down and waits with no time limit; only an interrupt of the closing thread makes it call shutdownNow().
basis: section:shutdown() Stops Intake, Not Work: Wait for It With awaitTermination()
aspects.reason: a test of an unbounded wait can only show it by waiting out a time limit; the drain practice grades the bounded stop the page recommends instead

aspects.says: A task run with execute() that throws ends its worker thread and reaches the uncaught-exception handler; one run with submit() has its exception stored in the Future, where only get() shows it.
basis: section:execute() Hands a Task's Exception to the Thread; submit() Keeps It in the Future

aspects.says: A fixed pool's size also limits how many calls reach a downstream at once; the cached pool and the virtual-thread executor have no such limit, so the call itself needs one.
basis: section:A Pool's Size Is Also a Limit on Concurrency, and Some Executors Have None

aspects.says: A ThreadPoolExecutor starts core threads first, then queues, and starts threads past the core only when the queue refuses a task; with an unbounded queue the maximum is never used.
basis: section:A Pool Queues Before It Grows: Threads Past the Core Start Only When the Queue Is Full

aspects.says: A bounded pool hands a task it cannot take to its policy: AbortPolicy throws to the submitter, CallerRunsPolicy runs it on the submitting thread, and the discard policies drop a task silently.
basis: section:A Full Pool Has to Refuse Work: Bound the Queue and Choose Who Pays

aspects.says: shutdown() refuses new tasks and returns at once while running and queued tasks still run; awaitTermination waits, and shutdownNow() is the fallback when it times out.
basis: section:shutdown() Stops Intake, Not Work: Wait for It With awaitTermination()

aspects.says: newFixedThreadPool queues without a limit, so work that arrives faster than it is done waits in memory until the heap runs out.
basis: section:A Pool Queues Before It Grows: Threads Past the Core Start Only When the Queue Is Full
